problems.problem: The contact detail crop (462,1098)-(979,1348) shows the bottle base resting on the floor with a faint soft shading line under the base, but the contact cue is very weak for a dark glossy bottle on a light matte floor; the shadow reads as ambient occlusion rather than a committed contact shadow, slightly weakening the grounded feel.

Compared with the three references, which use layered set design (florals, drapery, tonal depth, bold integrated typography), this poster is a single isolated bottle on a flat sage field. The references achieve depth via foreground/midground layering and typographic scale contrast; here the composition is competent but generic and lacks a signature element beyond the leaf shadows.

The left text block (logo/title/subtitle confined to x 84-452, small sizes 20-40px) is disconnected in scale from the large hero bottle (55% of canvas height); the upper-left quadrant feels sparse while the bottle dominates the right-center, producing an unbalanced visual weight without an anchoring graphic device.

Title at 40px in Times reads generic against the luxury references (Dior's oversized serif headline, Jo Malone's tracked caps); hierarchy between logo 26px / title 40px / subtitle 20px is too compressed and lacks letter-spacing refinement expected in a luxury campaign.

changes.value: Empty pale sage green matte seamless studio environment, continuous floor and wall with a soft far tonal transition, warm soft diffuse frontal light with a gentle directional falloff from the right, delicate out-of-focus leaf and thin branch shadows at the far left and upper right edges only, a low calm pool of brighter light on the floor at the center right where the hero sits, quiet airy organic still-life atmosphere, no furniture
